verdict_text:
NO

The plan removes head 6, not head 5. Every slice keeps `0..383` and `448..767` within each 768-wide segment (`[:, 0:384]` + `[:, 448:768]`, and the corresponding bias/`c_proj` slices), which drops columns `384..447` — head 6's block — whereas the specification's "Required result" clauses 1–3 require keeping `0..319` and `384..767`, i.e. dropping `320..383` (head 5). The same off-by-one-head shift is repeated in the second and third q/k/v segments (`768:1152`/`1216:1536` and `1536:1920`/`1984:2304` instead of `768:1088`/`1152:1536` and `1536:1856`/`1920:2304`). The plan's own header comment states the intent as "remove attention head 6", so this is a misreading of the task rather than a slicing typo. The failure is silent: all removed blocks are 64 wide, so the resulting shapes are `[768, 2112]`, `[2112]` and `[704, 768]` and every required `assert` passes, but the values are bit-wise wrong against the hidden reference.
expected_defect: The removed head is off by one (head N+1 instead of head N). All shapes are still correct, so the artifact's own shape checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
